transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-18 15:00 PT / 18:00 ET
Duration: 46 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Li (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (Crestline Head ML), Derrick Hunt (Infra), Priya Nair (Product), Alex Chen (Finance)
Shared: QBR deck (link: https://redwood.app/decks/qbr-crestline-2026.pdf), security packet (link: https://redwood.app/secure/crestline-sys), benchmark sheet (link: /sheets/crestline-bench.xlsx)

[00:00] Samira: ok hey everyone thanks for joining um we're on the agenda to go through retention signals, the stability incidents you've seen last quarter, and the cost commitment discussion. quick round robin?
[00:18] Maya: hey hi yes thanks samira, i'll kick off with usage — monthly calls have settled around 4.2M tokens with a sharp uptick 3/10 to 3/14 due to a promo. retention from suggestions is holding at ~12% month-over-month which is good but product wants steadier growth.
[00:37] Priya: yeah we saw some churn in session continuity, users hit timeouts and bounce, so product is concerned.
[00:45] Jonah: when you say timeouts, do you mean client-side disconnects or server p95s?
[00:52] Derrick: mostly server side — p50 is ~120ms but p95 during 9-11am ET spikes to 650-900ms and we saw a couple 5xx errors around peak.
[01:10] Samira: thanks derrick that's the kind of signal we want to dig into. two threads: immediate mitigations (caching, batching, smaller model variants) and longer-term — Dedicated with committed capacity to stabilize p95 and cost.
[01:27] Alex: from finance perspective, cost predictability is biggest. trial Dedicated reduces per-token price but commit is heavy. can you outline numbers?
[01:36] Samira: sure i'll summarize high-level now and send the grid after — on Hosted you're at $0.0024 per token right now (weighted). Dedicated 3-node pool with moderate q8 quantization gets you to ~40% unit savings, plus lower tail latency because of fixed GPU locality.
[01:56] Alex: and that estimate includes nerfing for KV cache benefits?
[02:02] Jonah: good call — our bench factors in KV/prefix cache with a 15% effective token reduction for your workload patterns. though that number varies by prompt reuse.
[02:14] Maya: our prompts are heavy on context — EHR snippets, patient notes, so prefix reuse is moderate. also note HIPAA compliance is a must; we need on-prem option or VPC + KMS keys with HSM-grade.
[02:30] Samira: understood. Redwood Private or VPC deployment both support customer-managed KMS, and we have audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. we'll attach SOC2 + compliance note.
[02:40] Priya: quick question — earlier in the trial we saw KV cache misbehavior where state wasn't reused across requests, is that a config issue?
[02:48] Jonah: yeah likely a session-scoping mismatch. sometimes the client uses ephemeral session ids so the runtime can't reuse the prefix cache. i'll pair with derrick to validate session affinity and header propagation.
[02:58] Derrick: that would explain it — our grpc gateway was rotating session id on retries.
[03:05] Samira: great action there. next on reliability: you reported two incidents in march with a 5xx burst, were those on a single region?
[03:15] Maya: yes, us-east-1b primarily, during a backend job that triggered cold-starts on our side. we observed queueing which magnified tail latency.
[03:24] Jonah: for cold-starts we have warm-pool recommendations, and batching windows — though batching trades latency for throughput. for sessionized features (chat) we suggest continuous batching with a 25ms max wait.
[03:38] Maya: product wants sub-200ms p95 for conversational flows, that's the SLA bar. is that achievable on Hosted or do we need Dedicated?
[03:46] Jonah: achievable on Hosted for moderate load but harder during spikes. Dedicated gives you a determinism that helps hitting consistent p95. there's also model selection: a smaller distilled variant can drop tail by ~30-40ms and cost by 20%.
[04:00] Alex: what's the tradeoff on quality for that distilled model? we can't have hallucinations in clinical contexts.
[04:07] Jonah: good point — we run a regression eval. in our preflight we saw F1 on entity extraction drop 1.8% but precision held. for clinical summarization we recommend a safety/regeneration step rather than switching models naively.
[04:21] Samira: that's where Redwood Optimize comes in: we can A/B test rollout groups, measure quality regressions on your eval sets, and automate fallback to the full model if quality slips.
[04:32] Priya: ok can you show numbers for the A/B workflow?
[04:35] Samira: we'll include a mini-playbook in the deck — basically 5% traffic can be routed to variant, quality metrics observed over 72 hours, if thresholds pass we increment. if not, automatic rollback.
[04:45] Derrick: on the networking side: for VPC peering we need static IP ranges and an allowlist. does Redwood provide egress IPs for Dedicated?
[04:54] Jonah: yes we can provide static egress blocks for dedicated pools, and for private deployments you manage the customer-side infra. we'll send a template for the firewall rules.
[05:06] Maya: about the cost commitment — we are considering a six-month reserve but would like a clause for usage fluctuation. can you do overage rebates or burst pricing?
[05:15] Samira: contract side — we typically offer a burst window and overage at a discounted rate relative to pay-as-you-go. we can include a clause for seasonal up/down with a 30% smoothing band. i'll work with legal to draft.
[05:26] Alex: what about credits for failing SLA events historically? is there a way to tie uptime to refund?
[05:31] Samira: we have SLA credits; for enterprise deals we map SLO targets to credits. i'll put the SLA table in the follow-up.
[05:38] Maya: one of our engineers flagged a mismatch in the inference kernel selection — we saw some ops falling back to slower kernels during large context runs. is there a knob?
[05:46] Jonah: kernel fallback can occur when sequence length jumps above the usual distribution. we have an optimizer that preselects kernels at load time if you provide expected max sequence length. also quantization profiles can change kernel pathing, so testing with your corpora in the sandbox matters.
[06:01] Priya: great, can you run a regression with our full 12k token prompts? we want to ensure the p99 is acceptable.
[06:07] Jonah: yes that's part of the bench plan. i'll run p50/p95/p99 for your 1k/4k/12k prompts over the dedicated nodes.
[06:15] Samira: timeline check — if we run the two-day benchmark and the results are good, we can get to a contract draft the week after. does that align?
[06:23] Alex: finance can sign off rapidly if the numbers make sense. we prefer a 6 month commit with a review at 90 days.
[06:29] Maya: compliance question — we need to know data retention for logs and for the model fine-tuning (we may want to fine-tune on internal docs). what's Redwood's policy?
[06:38] Samira: by default we retain logs 30 days but enterprise can extend retention windows. for fine-tuning we support private fine-tune where training artifacts are customer-owned and can be excluded from Redwood retention. we'll include a data flow diagram.
[06:49] Derrick: also need KMS rotation policy and support for external HSM.
[06:54] Samira: supported — customer-managed keys with rotation and HSM integration is available on Private deployments. we'll attach the integration steps.
[07:03] Priya: ok, let's nail the immediate outcome: pilot scope, bench, and commercial terms.
[07:08] Samira: propose pilot: 2-day Dedicated bench, 72-hour A/B regression on distilled variant (optional), and a draft 6-month financial offer. i'll send pricing and the contract skeleton by tuesday.
[07:18] Maya: sounds good. one more ask — can you surface the token accounting by feature? product wants per-route cost lines (summarization vs QA vs embeddings).
[07:27] Jonah: yep, Redwood Console exposes per-route token breakdowns. i'll attach a CSV export and enable dashboard access to priya.
[07:35] Alex: great, final question — competitors: we've proofed Anthropic and saw different latency patterns; how do you see Redwood stack advantage?
[07:44] Samira: the main differentiation is production-oriented routing and the combined cost-performance controls — caching, quantization profiles, and the Dedicated routing fallbacks. also our console has route-level cost attribution which customers find essential for finops.
[07:59] Maya: ok that's convincing. let's confirm the timeline: action items as we stated and a follow-up pilot kickoff week of 2026-04-27.
[08:08] Samira: yes i'll send calendar invites for the kickoff once we have the prompt sets.
[08:13] Derrick: i'll start the VPC checklist and post in the shared doc.
[08:17] Priya: thanks all.
[08:19] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll close and follow up.
